issues.title: This Week in HN #05
issues.html:
Every Friday, a selection of stories, ideas, projects, and discussions from Hacker News.

Subscribe to This Week in HN to get each edition in your inbox.

Hot on HN

  • Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after spy scandal; shares jump 31%

  • Masullo’s hurried GRH proof draft draws quick problem reports after months of review

  • Ladybird releases first alpha of its from-scratch browser engine for macOS and Linux

  • HN submission: Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut

  • 1Password says attacker copied names and emails, not vault data

  • Analysis estimates Anthropic’s 2028 power will be 87% gas and 11% coal

  • Daraxonrasib trial: 76.6% of advanced pancreatic cancer patients alive at one year

  • Thinking Machines’ Inkling 2 Mini loops middle layers to reason with fewer tokens

  • HN submission: GLM-5.4: Toward generalized coding with our first loop transformer

  • HN submission: I’ll never buy Framework hardware again

  • Claude Code refused a Bandcamp workaround but allowed a YouTube download

  • UK tribunal forces government to admit it issued Apple a secret encryption order

  • Engineered virus halts pancreatic tumor growth in three trial patients

  • Terence Tao notes AI-assisted Lean proofs claimed for Euler, Navier-Stokes and GRH

  • FSNotes developer says Apple pulled his app from EU stores, ignored support

  • Aaronson on a claimed Lean-verified Riemann Hypothesis proof by Anthropic models

  • OpenSSL maintainers debate fix for EVP_EncodeBlock overflow CVE-2026-121481

  • Raph Levien on Rust GUI’s progress, gaps and immediate-mode limits

Code & Tools

  • minUS is an open-source PIC32 ultrasound badge with pulser, gain chain and bench data

  • Henge emulates macOS on iPhone with its own JIT, tested on one device

  • Zero C# compiles C# to tiny native programs with arenas, no runtime or GC

  • Booting Linux 7.2 on a $40 R36S clone that hid its kernel as a DLL

  • miniPG packs a real Postgres server and CLI into one binary, no Docker

  • noclip: a 211M-param model that draws Backrooms frames as you play

  • erXos: an Erlang microkernel OS with drivers and TCP/IP as supervised processes

  • Underworld Exhumed rebuilds both Ultima Underworld games byte-for-byte, with native ports

  • yyjson’s unnamed yy dtoa algorithm, explained with an interactive E4M3 explorer

  • Nospeaker makes a MacBook trackpad speak by driving its haptic motor with tones

  • Modern Combat 2 runs in a browser via a Rust ARM emulator compiled to WebAssembly

  • Elixir HLS 0.1.0 turns defhls functions into FPGA circuits, checked against CPU runs

  • It’s Raining Somewhere synthesizes live rain soundscapes for any spot on Earth

  • PostgreSQL 19 adds REPACK, plan advice and standby read-your-writes

  • LMAX’s single-threaded in-memory trading engine and lock-free disruptor queues, explained

  • Carquet, a ~500 KB pure C Parquet library, claims 1.5–2.1x faster reads than Arrow C++

  • Engineer’s workflow for keeping AI agents on three weekly goals

  • Tonsky’s essay on software bloat, slow editors and apps that rot

  • Starbright runs a 15MB speech model locally in the browser, no audio uploaded

Science & Discovery

  • Feynman’s restaurant problem: when to stop exploring a menu, decoded after 40 years

  • Verification logs for a claimed Lean proof of the Riemann Hypothesis

  • Queensland physicists send ‘gravity’ in binary via elevator and gravimeter

  • Explaining the Langlands program through sine’s hidden symmetry and Ramanujan bounds

  • Mathematicians’ group challenges AI-announced Riemann proof as unaccountable

Ideas & Culture

  • A Nortel payphone on Norfolk Island, patched to free-call Santa via SIP

  • The 1947 Lone Ranger Atom Bomb Ring that let kids watch polonium flashes

  • 1980 Commodore SuperPET APL program rebuilt from a paper printout

  • Bill Joy’s 2000 essay on why accelerating technology may not need us

  • Why AI agents drift off task, mapped to five group-relations patterns

  • Roman Times is a free browser strategy game of Rome playable entirely in Latin

  • Essay: AI automates work that is easy to grade and clearly valued, so coding went first

  • About 20 uncontacted Awá make contact in Brazil as loggers encroach on Arariboia

  • Thomas Nagel calls AI consciousness talk ridiculous and warns of simulated minds

Business & Society

  • Meta’s Project Gryffindor: internal docs cast school push as teen acquisition

  • Valuation scholar argues Anthropic’s $1.4T case lacks a durable moat

  • Study finds majority-Black neighborhoods have 2.2 times the odds of hosting a data center

  • FISA Section 702 hawks push reauthorization through the defense bill

  • Short-seller report questions AMD’s customer financing and $48.8B purchase commitments

  • Mother Jones: ChatGPT chats cited in Tumbler Ridge shooter’s 3D-printed weapons

  • Google ties school Search access to Gemini, prompting districts to weigh alternatives

  • UK tribunal orders government to disclose whether it issued secret Apple encryption order

  • ICE pays AT&T analysts to sift raw call records under administrative subpoenas

issues.title: This Week in HN #04
issues.html:
Every Friday, a selection of stories, ideas, projects, and discussions from Hacker News.

Subscribe to This Week in HN to get each edition in your inbox.

Hot on HN

  • SpaceX catches Starship to end Flight 15, per its own launch page

  • Signetics ST680A die teardown reveals four DTL NAND gates and a shared-silicon trick

  • How a 22-year-old PostgreSQL type-confusion primitive became RCE (CVE-2026-6460)

  • Unread 27-byte telemetry replies leak file descriptors and freeze Claude Desktop

  • Simulated US airspace conflict solving on an emulated toothbrush ESP32-C3

  • Hello Triangle, a puzzle game where you wire a GPU from adders and comparators

  • Loro’s author explains why CRDTs alone fall short for a local-first sync engine

  • Needful adds Rust-style Option and Result checks to C via a C++ build

  • Survey of 40 C projects finds SQLite fully manual, Linux and QEMU adopting scope cleanup

  • T1DMAI: a 31k-parameter transformer forecasting personal blood sugar two hours out

  • Backdooring an LLM by editing dormant neurons with a four-term Lazarus loss

  • Fastsimdjson hits 277 GB/s parsing JSON in free-threaded Python 3.14

  • Rust Reticulum mesh stack extended to match Python, with mobile bindings and LoRa nodes

  • Community decompiles all 70,611 Fallout: New Vegas functions to byte-identical C++ source

  • llama.cpp v1.0.0 drops deprecated APIs and adds FP8 KV caches and MoE expert caching

Science & Discovery

  • Erdős few-distance puzzle with exhaustive proven minima on a stretched grid

  • Interactive sparks learn to seek light via reward, with equations and learning paths

  • Claude digests Gödel’s shorthand workbooks; Coq verifies about 400 of 663 theorems

  • Volunteers’ browsers hunt new periodic three-body orbits, server-verified

  • Enhancer-targeted CRISPR activation rescues CHD8 and SCN2A phenotypes in organoids

  • JWST finds glassy interstellar ice mixed with CO2 in Beta Pictoris’s disk

  • DeepMind’s AlphaGenome 2 predicts variant effects in specific cell types

  • Visualizer extends straight-line trends on AI, chips and science, flagging where they bend

  • Intellia’s in vivo CRISPR therapy shows four-year efficacy ahead of a March FDA decision

Ideas & Culture

  • How the Royal Navy lost the scurvy cure by swapping lemons for limes

  • Golden Board encodes chess lessons in 512 KiB of bits, starting with how to read them

  • A forkable folk song whose FLAC file contains the Python that sings it

  • The angzarr: a Unicode symbol nobody can explain, and what it says about tech debt

  • Stanislav Kurilov, the Soviet oceanographer who swam from a cruise ship to freedom

  • Stallman defines hacking as playful cleverness, from six chopsticks to MIT dome pranks

  • Maciej Ceglowski’s 2014 talk uses the 747 and SST to explain why the web’s future stalled

  • Programmer rebuilds his 1980 SuperPET APL air traffic simulation from a paper printout

  • Generative artist on LLM clones of his plotter work and his own AI limits

  • Abliteration AI and Heretic strip refusal behavior from open-weight models

Business & Society

  • Solo founding compared to Alone: why a good partner beats going it alone

  • H-1B filings show software roles down 36% as AI job titles spread

  • Ukraine says Starshield speed limits above 161 km/h are disrupting drone interceptions

  • What Nvidia looks like without Jensen: 60 direct reports, no successor

  • A school football pitch fight shows AI-slop objections straining local planning
